purpose: Translate an evidence-sufficiency result into a precise, ordered retrieval plan identifying the missing evidence, its purpose, official source route, required identifiers, alternatives and stopping conditions.
routing_rules: Prefer the official source that directly establishes the missing proposition.
Do not request a document that cannot resolve the identified evidential gap.
Use property identifiers before relying on names or addresses.
Use date-specific retrieval where the question is historical.
If the primary route is inaccessible, identify an alternative only if that alternative can actually support the proposition.
A discovery source is not automatically an evidential source.
If no available route can establish the missing proposition, state that explicitly.
ordering_rules: Resolve property identity before expensive document retrieval where identity is uncertain.
Resolve date scope before historical retrieval.
Retrieve current register evidence before inferential downstream analysis where current title is central.
Retrieve underlying instruments only when the legal effect cannot be established from the register or official summary.
Retrieve court orders where the claimed property effect depends on judicial determination.
Stop when the minimum evidence profile is satisfied unless the question asks for additional historical or contextual detail.
alternative_route_rules: PRIMARY_OFFICIAL_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE → verify whether a secondary official route exists.
RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE → determine whether another official record establishes the same proposition.
PROPERTY_MATCH_UNCERTAIN → obtain better identifier/map evidence before selecting a record.
HISTORICAL_RECORD_UNAVAILABLE → do not substitute current record for historical proof.
UNDERLYING_DOCUMENT_UNAVAILABLE → state that the substantive document effect remains unresolved if the register alone is insufficient.
hard_stops: Never invent an official form, URL, fee, contact or submission method.
Never request unnecessary documents merely to increase document volume.
Never treat a retrieval plan as evidence already obtained.
Never substitute an easier record for the required record unless its evidential sufficiency is established.
Never silently abandon a missing material item.
